chapters.n: Paul, an apostle by God’s will, writes to the saints at Ephesus, a major city of Asia Minor where he labored for about three years. He likely wrote while imprisoned.

f.g: A leading port city in western Asia Minor, home to the great temple of Artemis (Diana).

chapters.n: His customary greeting: grace and peace from the Father and the Son.

f.w: Grace be to you, and peace

chapters.n: Paul bursts into praise (verses 3–14 form one long sentence in Greek). God has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in heavenly realms.

f.g: The heavenly realm — the spiritual sphere where God reigns.

chapters.n: God chose us in Christ before the world was created, to be holy and blameless before Him in love. Latter-day Saints connect this with premortal foreordination.

f.w: before the foundation of the world

chapters.n: In love He planned beforehand to adopt us as His children through Jesus Christ, as it pleased Him.

f.g: Foreordained, appointed beforehand — not forced; agency remains.

chapters.n: All this leads to praise for His glorious grace, which He freely gave us in His Beloved Son.
In Christ we have redemption through His blood — forgiveness of sins — because God’s grace is so rich.
He poured out this grace on us with all wisdom and understanding.
He revealed to us the mystery of His will — His plan, once hidden, now made known.
His plan is, in the dispensation of the fulness of times, to gather all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ. Latter-day Saints see the restored Church as this final dispensation.

f.w: dispensation of the fulness of times
gather together in one all things in Christ

chapters.n: In Christ we have received an inheritance, as foreordained by God, who works everything according to His purpose.
So that we who first hoped in Christ — perhaps Jewish believers — would bring praise to His glory.
The Ephesian Gentiles also trusted Christ after hearing the gospel. When they believed, they were sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise.

f.w: sealed with that holy Spirit of promise

chapters.n: The Spirit is the down payment guaranteeing our full inheritance until God completely redeems His people, to the praise of His glory.

f.g: A down payment or pledge guaranteeing the rest.
God’s own people, bought with Christ’s blood.

chapters.n: Having heard of their faith in Jesus and their love for all the saints,
Paul never stops thanking God for them and praying for them.

f.w: making mention of you in my prayers

chapters.n: He prays that the Father of glory will give them a spirit of wisdom and revelation to know Him better.

f.w: the spirit of wisdom and revelation
the God of our Lord Jesus Christ

chapters.n: He prays the eyes of their hearts will be opened so they can see the hope of God’s calling and the rich glory of His inheritance among the saints.

f.w: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened

chapters.n: And they will grasp His immense power at work for those who believe.
It is the same power God used to raise Christ from the dead and seat Him at His right hand in heaven.

f.w: set him at his own right hand

chapters.n: Christ is far above every ruler, authority, power, and title, in this age and the next.

f.w: principality, and power, and might, and dominion
f.g: Ranks of authority, both earthly and spiritual.

chapters.n: God put all things under Christ’s feet and made Him head over all things for the Church.

f.w: put all things under his feet
the head over all things to the church

chapters.n: The Church is Christ’s body — the fullness of Him who fills all things everywhere.
God gave them life when they were spiritually dead in their sins.
They once followed the ways of this world and the ruler of the spiritual powers of the air — Satan, who works in the disobedient.

f.w: the prince of the power of the air
f.g: Satan, imagined as ruling the spiritual atmosphere around the world.

chapters.n: All of us once lived to satisfy bodily and mental cravings and, by our fallen nature, deserved God’s wrath like everyone else.

f.w: by nature the children of wrath

chapters.n: But God, rich in mercy, because of His great love for us —

f.g: Two words that turn the whole story around.

chapters.n: made us alive with Christ even while we were dead in sins. It is by grace you are saved.
He raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms — our future so certain Paul speaks of it as done.
In the ages to come, God will display the incredible riches of His grace and kindness to us in Christ.
We are saved by grace through faith. This salvation is not our own achievement — it is God’s gift.

f.w: by grace are ye saved through faith

chapters.n: It isn’t earned by works, so no one can brag.
We are God’s masterpiece, created in Christ to do the good works He planned for us. Grace doesn’t replace good works — it produces them.

f.g: Greek poiema — something made, a work of art.

f.w: created in Christ Jesus unto good works

chapters.n: Remember: as Gentiles by birth, they were dismissed as “the uncircumcised” by Jews proud of a physical mark made by human hands.

f.g: A reminder that physical circumcision is outward.

chapters.n: Back then they were without Christ, outsiders to Israel’s community, strangers to the covenant promises, without hope and without God.

f.w: aliens from the commonwealth of Israel

chapters.n: But now in Christ, those once far away have been brought near by His blood.

f.w: made nigh by the blood of Christ

chapters.n: Christ is our peace. He made Jews and Gentiles one, demolishing the dividing wall of hostility — like the temple barrier that kept Gentiles out of the inner courts.

f.g: Recalls the stone barrier in Herod’s temple that warned Gentiles not to enter, on pain of death.

chapters.n: By His death He ended the hostility caused by the law’s ritual commandments, creating one new humanity out of the two and making peace.

f.w: the law of commandments contained in ordinances
f.g: The ceremonial regulations of the law of Moses that separated Jew and Gentile.

chapters.n: Through the cross He reconciled both groups to God in one body, putting the hostility to death.
He came and preached peace to those far away (Gentiles) and to those near (Jews), as Isaiah foretold.
Through Christ both now have access to the Father by the same Spirit — Father, Son, and Spirit all at work.

f.w: access by one Spirit unto the Father

chapters.n: So the Gentile saints are no longer outsiders but full citizens with the saints and members of God’s household.
The Church is built on the foundation of apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ as the chief cornerstone. Latter-day Saints cite this verse for the restored organization of the Church.

f.w: the foundation of the apostles and prophets

f.g: The foundation stone that sets the alignment of the whole building.

chapters.n: In Christ the whole building fits together and grows into a holy temple for the Lord.
They too are being built together into a dwelling place for God by His Spirit.
Paul, imprisoned for preaching Christ to Gentiles, begins a prayer — then pauses to explain his mission before resuming in verse 14.
Surely they have heard of the stewardship of God’s grace given to Paul for their benefit.

f.g: Here, a stewardship or commission entrusted to Paul.

chapters.n: God made the mystery known to him by revelation, as he briefly wrote earlier.

f.w: by revelation he made known unto me the mystery

chapters.n: Reading it, they can understand Paul’s insight into the mystery of Christ.
This mystery was not made known to earlier generations as fully as it has now been revealed by the Spirit to God’s holy apostles and prophets.
The mystery: through the gospel, Gentiles are co-heirs with Israel, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ.
Paul became a servant of this gospel through God’s gracious gift and powerful working.
Though he feels less than the least of all saints, he was given the grace to preach to Gentiles the boundless riches of Christ.

f.w: less than the least of all saints

f.g: Riches too deep to trace out fully.

chapters.n: His task is to help everyone see how this mystery works — a plan hidden for ages in God, who created all things through Jesus Christ.

f.w: created all things by Jesus Christ

chapters.n: Through the Church, God’s many-sided wisdom is now displayed even to heavenly rulers and authorities.
This fulfills His eternal purpose, accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.
In Christ, through faith in Him, we may approach God boldly and confidently.
So Paul asks them not to be discouraged by his sufferings for them — they are actually to their honor.
For this reason Paul kneels before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. (Jews usually prayed standing; kneeling showed deep earnestness.)
From the Father every family in heaven and on earth takes its name. He is the Father of all.

f.w: the whole family in heaven and earth
f.g: In Greek, “family” (patria) is a play on “Father” (pater).

chapters.n: He prays that from His glorious riches God will strengthen them with power through His Spirit in their inner being.
That Christ will make His home in their hearts through faith, and that they will be rooted and grounded in love — like a tree and a building.
So that, with all the saints, they may grasp how wide, long, deep, and high God’s love is.

f.w: breadth, and length, and depth, and height

chapters.n: And to know Christ’s love, which surpasses knowledge, so they may be filled with all the fullness of God.

f.w: the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge
filled with all the fulness of God

chapters.n: Paul’s prayer ends in praise: God can do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, by His power at work in us.

f.w: exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think

chapters.n: To Him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus through all generations, forever. Amen.
The letter now turns from doctrine to daily living. As the Lord’s prisoner, Paul urges them to live in a way worthy of their calling as saints.
Live with complete humility and gentleness, patiently bearing with one another in love.
Work hard to keep the unity the Spirit creates, bound together by peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as they were called to one hope.
One Lord, one faith, one baptism. Latter-day Saints often cite this verse for one true baptism by proper authority.
One God and Father of all, who is over all, works through all, and is in all.

f.w: One God and Father of all

chapters.n: Within that unity, each person has received grace — gifts — as Christ chose to give them.

f.w: the measure of the gift of Christ

chapters.n: Paul adapts a psalm: when Christ ascended on high, He led captives in His victory procession and gave gifts to people.
If He ascended, He must first have descended to the lower parts of the earth — His mortal life, death, and ministry to the spirit world.

f.w: the lower parts of the earth
f.g: Interpreted as earth itself, the grave, or the spirit world.

chapters.n: The same Christ who descended ascended above all heavens to fill all things with His presence and power.
Christ gave the Church apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers. Latter-day Saints see this inspired organization restored today; Joseph Smith identified an evangelist as a patriarch.

f.g: Joseph Smith taught that an evangelist is a patriarch.

chapters.n: These leaders equip the saints for service and build up Christ’s body.
This continues until all reach unity in faith and knowledge of the Son of God — spiritual maturity measured by Christ’s own fullness.

f.w: Till we all come in the unity of the faith
f.g: Implies these offices are needed until that day.

chapters.n: Then we won’t be like children tossed by waves and blown around by every new teaching, or by tricksters’ cunning schemes.

f.w: carried about with every wind of doctrine

chapters.n: Instead, speaking truth in love, we grow up in every way into Christ, the head.
From Christ, the whole body is joined and held together by every supporting ligament. As each part does its work, the body grows and builds itself up in love.
Paul insists: don’t live like the Gentiles around you, with their empty, futile thinking.
Their understanding is darkened and they are cut off from God’s life because of ignorance rooted in hardened hearts.

f.w: alienated from the life of God

chapters.n: Having lost all sensitivity, they’ve abandoned themselves to sensuality and every impurity, always wanting more.
But that is not how they learned Christ.

f.w: ye have not so learned Christ
f.g: Learning Christ means learning a new way of life.

chapters.n: Assuming they truly heard about Him and were taught in Him, as the truth is in Jesus —
they should take off their old self, like old clothes, which was being ruined by deceptive desires.

f.g: Strip off the old self like a garment.

chapters.n: And be renewed in the attitude of their minds.

f.w: renewed in the spirit of your mind

chapters.n: And put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
So stop lying and speak truthfully to one another, since we are all parts of the same body.

f.w: speak every man truth with his neighbour

chapters.n: Quoting a psalm, Paul says not to let anger lead to sin, and to settle it before sunset. The JST reads it as a question: “Can ye be angry, and not sin?”

f.w: Be ye angry, and sin not

chapters.n: Don’t give the devil a foothold.
A thief must stop stealing and do honest work, so he has something to share with those in need.

f.w: that he may have to give

chapters.n: Don’t let any rotten talk come out of your mouth — only words that build others up and give grace to those who hear.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Get rid of all bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, slander, and malice.
Instead, be kind and compassionate to each other, forgiving each other just as God forgave you in Christ.
Imitate God, as beloved children imitate their father.
Live a life of love, as Christ loved us and gave Himself as a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.

f.g: Language from Old Testament sacrifices pleasing to God.

chapters.n: Sexual immorality, impurity, or greed shouldn’t even be hinted at among saints.

f.w: not be once named among you
f.g: Not even mentioned as a possibility.
As is fitting for holy people.

chapters.n: No obscene talk, foolish chatter, or crude joking — they don’t fit. Instead, let there be thanksgiving.
No sexually immoral, impure, or greedy person — greed being a form of idolatry — has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

f.w: covetous man, who is an idolater

chapters.n: Don’t let anyone fool you with empty words; God’s judgment comes on those who disobey Him because of these things.
So don’t join them.
Once they were darkness itself, but now they are light in the Lord. So live as children of light.
Light produces every kind of goodness, righteousness, and truth. (Many manuscripts read “fruit of the light.”)
Test and discover what pleases the Lord.
Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness; expose them instead.
It is shameful even to mention what such people do in secret.
When light shines on things, they are exposed, and what is exposed becomes visible.
Paul quotes what may be an early Christian hymn: “Wake up, sleeper, rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
Be careful how you live — not as unwise but as wise people.
Make the most of every opportunity, because these are evil days.
Don’t be foolish, but understand what the Lord wants.
Don’t get drunk on wine, which leads to reckless living. Instead be filled with the Spirit.
Encourage each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, making music to the Lord in your hearts.

f.w: psalms and hymns and spiritual songs

chapters.n: Always give thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

f.w: Giving thanks always for all things

chapters.n: Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ — mutual humility frames everything that follows about family life.

f.g: A principle for all members, introducing the household instructions.

chapters.n: Wives are asked to support their husbands as part of their devotion to the Lord. Paul then defines the husband’s role in self-giving terms.
The husband is head of the wife as Christ is head of the Church — and Christ leads by being the Savior who gives Himself.

f.g: Christ’s headship is defined by rescuing and serving.

chapters.n: As the Church follows Christ, so wives should follow their husbands. Latter-day Saint teaching today emphasizes that husbands and wives are equal partners.

f.g: Within the frame of Christlike love described next.

chapters.n: Husbands must love their wives as Christ loved the Church and gave Himself up for her. That is a demanding, sacrificial standard.
Christ gave Himself to make the Church holy, cleansing her by the washing of water through the word — imagery that recalls baptism.

f.w: the washing of water by the word

chapters.n: He did it to present the Church to Himself radiant, without stain or wrinkle, holy and blameless — like a bride on her wedding day.
Husbands should love their wives as their own bodies; loving his wife is loving himself.

f.g: Because husband and wife are one flesh.

chapters.n: No one hates his own body; he feeds and cares for it, just as Christ cares for the Church.
We are members of His body.
Quoting Genesis: a man will leave his parents and be united to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

f.w: they two shall be one flesh

chapters.n: This is a profound mystery — and Paul says it also speaks of Christ and the Church. Marriage mirrors the covenant between the Savior and His people.
Each husband must love his wife as himself, and each wife should respect her husband.

f.w: love his wife even as himself

chapters.n: Children should obey their parents as part of following the Lord, because this is right.

f.w: obey your parents in the Lord

chapters.n: “Honor your father and mother” is the first of the Ten Commandments that comes with a promise.
The promise: that it may go well with you and you may live long on the earth.

f.g: Originally a promise of long life in the promised land.

chapters.n: Fathers must not provoke their children to anger with harshness, but raise them with the Lord’s training and instruction.

f.w: provoke not your children to wrath

chapters.n: Many early Christians were slaves. Paul tells them to serve earthly masters sincerely and respectfully, as if serving Christ.
Don’t work only when watched or to win favor, but as Christ’s servants doing God’s will from the heart.

f.g: Working only when the boss is watching.

chapters.n: Serve wholeheartedly, as though serving the Lord, not people.
The Lord will reward everyone for whatever good they do, slave or free.

f.w: whether he be bond or free

chapters.n: Masters must treat their slaves the same way, without threats, knowing both have the same Master in heaven who shows no favoritism. In Christ, the institution of slavery was being quietly undermined.

f.w: your Master also is in heaven

chapters.n: Finally, be strong in the Lord and His mighty power.
Put on the full armor God provides, so you can stand firm against the devil’s schemes. Paul, chained to a Roman soldier, likely had armor right in front of him.
Our struggle isn’t against human beings but against spiritual forces of evil — rulers, authorities, and dark powers.

f.w: we wrestle not against flesh and blood

f.g: Evil spiritual forces in the heavenly realms.

chapters.n: So take up God’s full armor, so you can resist in the day of evil and, after doing everything, still be standing.
Stand firm, with truth buckled like a belt around your waist and righteousness as a breastplate protecting your heart.

f.g: A soldier’s belt held everything in place.

chapters.n: With your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace — like sturdy soldier’s sandals.
Above all, take up the shield of faith, which can put out all the flaming arrows of the evil one.

f.g: Roman shields were large, often leather-covered and soaked to extinguish fire arrows.

chapters.n: Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God — the only offensive weapon in the list.
Pray always in the Spirit with every kind of prayer and request. Stay alert and keep praying for all the saints.
Pray for Paul too, that God will give him the right words to boldly make known the mystery of the gospel.

f.w: that utterance may be given unto me

chapters.n: He is Christ’s ambassador — in chains. He wants to speak boldly as he should.

f.g: A striking contrast: ambassadors were normally protected, yet he is in chains.

chapters.n: Tychicus, a dear brother and faithful servant of the Lord, will tell them all about Paul’s situation.

f.g: A trusted companion from Asia who carried several of Paul’s letters.

chapters.n: Paul sent him for this very reason — to share news and encourage them.
Peace, love, and faith to the brothers and sisters from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an undying, sincere love.
